channel.title: Honolulu Civil Beat - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Honolulu Civil Beat (civilbeat.org)

item.title: DOE Made Little Progress Last Year On Local Food Goals
item.description: School leaders say spending on local products will increase once the DOE opens a regional kitchen in Wahiawā in 2027, but the department is nowhere near meeting its legislatively mandated goals.

item.title: Makana Eyre: Hawaiʻi-Style Canoe Paddling Has Spread Worldwide
item.description: About 20% of the members of this New York canoe club have Hawaiʻi roots.

item.title: Word Flower: Feb. 2
item.description: Lots of words to find today so start your week off right.

item.title: A Cure For Sour Feelings About Politics? Get People To Love Their Hometowns
item.description: The positive feelings people have toward their community translate directly into civic engagement.

item.title: State Agrees To Settle Case Over Prison Drug Withdrawal Death
item.description: The settlement calls for a $600,000 payment to the estate of Brian Kimo O'Gorman after he suffered heart failure while withdrawing from methadone.

item.title: Oceanfront Lahaina Property Owners May Get Buyout In Updated Disaster Plan
item.description: The county is seeking an amendment to create a voluntary buyout program with some of its $1.6 billion fire recovery grant from the feds.

item.title: It’s Time To Reconsider Disclosure Requirements For UH Regents
item.description: The strength of the University of Hawaiʻi depends on who is willing to serve.

item.title: Ed Case Has Substantial Lead In Money Race For U.S. House Seat
item.description: But state Rep. Jarrett Keohokalole has mounted a strong challenge and has attracted significant donors.

item.title: US Education Department Paid Up To $38 Million To Civil Rights Workers On Leave
item.description: Nearly half the staff of the Office of Civil Rights was placed on paid leave this spring.

item.title: The State Capitol Is Buzzing About This Prominent Hawaiʻi Lawmaker
item.description: Longtime Sen. Michelle Kidani may be leaving office early amid concerns about whether she is mentally fit.
